description: Acceptance of the bicycle example: the benchmark bicycle of Meijaard, Papadopoulos, Ruina and Schwab (Proc. R. Soc. A 463, 2007). The linear model is checked against the matrix exponential of the paper's matrices and the weave speed of table 2; the 3D multibond bond graph against the table 2 weave eigenvalues at 3 to 6 m/s, the linearised capsize growth at 8 m/s, the linear model at a small push (compare) and its own energy book.

checks.note: rear frame, fork and both wheels follow their composed body poses
compliant joints and explicit contacts: no derivative causality, connected and frame-consistent
the paper's figure 4 (same start: 4.6 m/s, lean rate 0.5 rad/s) plots the forward speed on a 4.60-4.70 m/s axis; measured 4.599 to 4.688 m/s (the figure is not tabulated, so this is only its range)
lower end of the figure 4 speed axis (measured 4.599)
self-stable at 4.6 m/s (between the weave speed 4.29 and the capsize speed 6.02 m/s): the lean of 0.116 rad after the push has decayed to at most 0.018 rad after 4 s
the rear tyre stays loaded (static 612.8 N; measured 588 to 623 N)
the front tyre stays loaded (static 309.3 N; measured 296 to 324 N)
rolling without slip up to a creep below 0.5 mm/s (measured 0.36 mm/s at the start: the lean rate turns the 0.7 mm deep contact point sideways)
longitudinal creep (measured 3.6 um/s)
energy book with the joint dampers on: E + tyre loss stays within 0.37 J of 1837 J (measured drift 0.24 J, the work of the dampers of the joints' held directions, not counted in the book)
joint dampers off: the Whipple bicycle is conservative, so kinetic + potential + tyre and joint springs + tyre loss is constant to 1.8 mJ in 1837 J (measured 0.07 mJ while the tyres dissipate 2.8 J)
